answer: CS 350 Compiler Design has one prerequisite: CS 250 Design and Analysis of Algorithms.

The Industry Internship (CS 499) is worth 6 credits and is an elective.

OS is CS 260 Operating Systems, and it meets in timetable slot B in Year 2, Semester 2.
Yes, CS 420 Information Retrieval (also called IR) is about how search engines work.
Its topics include indexing, ranking, BM25, vector search, and evaluation of search.
CS 420 is a 3-credit elective in the Data Science and AI and Machine Learning tracks, offered in Year 4, Semester 1, in timetable slot B.
Its prerequisites are CS 220 Database Systems and MA 201 Probability and Statistics.
You can register for it only after passing both prerequisites with a grade of P or better, and courses still in progress do not count as passed.
CS 345 Deep Learning is the course that teaches neural networks and backpropagation.
CS 345 is a 4-credit elective in the AI and Machine Learning track, offered in Year 3, Semester 2, in timetable slot D.
The prerequisite for CS 345 is CS 340 Machine Learning.
The course covers neural networks from backpropagation up to convolutional networks and transformers, and students train them in PyTorch.
CS 375 Cloud Computing is the course that covers containers and serverless computing.
The course teaches you how to run software in the cloud using containers, managed services, and serverless functions.
CS 375 is a 3-credit elective in the Systems track, offered in Year 3, Semester 2, in timetable slot E.
Before taking CS 375, you need to complete CS 260 Operating Systems and CS 270 Computer Networks.
CS 220 Database Systems (also called DBMS) is the course that covers SQL and transactions.
The course teaches students to design relational databases and query them with SQL, covering normalization, transactions, and indexes.
CS 220 is a 4-credit core course offered in Year 2, Semester 1, in timetable slot B, and its prerequisite is CS 102 Data Structures.
CS 410 Distributed Systems is the course for this, because its topics include replication and consensus.
CS 410 teaches how to build systems that keep working when they run on many machines and some parts fail.
CS 410 is a 3-credit Systems-track elective offered in Year 4, Semester 1, in timetable slot A.
Before taking CS 410, you need to have passed CS 260 Operating Systems and CS 270 Computer Networks.

The only listed prerequisite for CS 345 Deep Learning is CS 340 Machine Learning.
CS 340 Machine Learning in turn requires CS 250 Design and Analysis of Algorithms and MA 201 Probability and Statistics, so you need those before CS 340.
CS 340 is a core course offered in Year 3, Semester 1, and CS 345 is offered in Year 3, Semester 2.
CS 380 Natural Language Processing is the course that matches building a chatbot that understands typed text.
It covers text processing, word embeddings, language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation.
CS 380 is a 4-credit elective in the AI and Machine Learning and Data Science tracks, offered in Year 3, Semester 2.
Before taking CS 380, you need CS 340 Machine Learning.
CS 345 Deep Learning can also help, because it covers sequence models and transformers.
CS 345 runs in the same timetable slot as CS 380 (Year 3, Semester 2, slot D), so the two courses clash.
Yes, CS 430 Computer Vision teaches computers to understand images, including object detection.
Its topics include image formation, feature detection, convolutional networks, object detection, and segmentation.
CS 430 is a 4-credit elective in the AI and Machine Learning track, offered in Year 4, Semester 1, in timetable slot C.
To take CS 430 you first need CS 345 Deep Learning.
CS 345 Deep Learning in turn requires CS 340 Machine Learning, and it also covers convolutional networks.
CS 340 Machine Learning requires CS 250 Design and Analysis of Algorithms and MA 201 Probability and Statistics.
CS 385 Computer Security, also called cybersecurity, is the course that covers web security.
The course teaches how systems are attacked and how they are defended, with labs on web security and authentication.
CS 385 is a 3-credit elective in the Systems track, offered in Year 3, Semester 2, in timetable slot F.
To take CS 385, you must first complete CS 260 Operating Systems and CS 270 Computer Networks.
CS 270 Computer Networks, a core course, also covers HTTP and the basics of network security.

To take CS 460, you first need CS 340 Machine Learning and CS 360 Software Engineering. Your record wasn't shared, so I can't check whether you've completed them.
Yes, CS 450 Reinforcement Learning (RL) covers learning by trial and reward.
Its topics are Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Q-learning and policy gradients.
CS 450 is a 3-credit elective in the AI and Machine Learning track. It is offered in Year 4, Semester 2, in timetable slot A.
Before taking CS 450, you need to pass CS 340 Machine Learning and MA 201 Probability and Statistics.
Without special approval, the most you can register for is 20 credits in a semester, because a normal load is 9 to 20 credits.
If your CGPA is 8.0 or higher, you can ask for an overload of up to 24 credits in one semester.
An overload needs written approval from your faculty advisor before registration closes.
If your CGPA is below 8.0, you cannot overload, so your limit stays at 20 credits.
If you are on academic probation because your CGPA fell below 5.0, you can register for at most 16 credits, and you must meet your faculty advisor before registering.
Yes, a prerequisite can be waived, but the decision is made jointly by the course's instructor and the head of department.
A waiver is available only to students who show equivalent preparation.
Waivers are rare, and Capstone Project II never gets one.
Without a waiver, you can register for a course only after passing every listed prerequisite with a grade of P or better, and courses still in progress don't count as passed.
If you fail a core course, you get an F, which is worth 0 grade points and earns no credits.
You have to repeat a failed core course the next time it is offered, which is the same semester of the following year.
When you pass the course on a later attempt, the new grade replaces the F in your CGPA.
Until you pass the failed course, you cannot register for any course that lists it as a prerequisite, because prerequisites must be passed with a grade of P or better.
You must pass every core course before you can graduate.
You haven't shared your record, so this is the general rule and not a check of your own courses.
To graduate, you need to pass at least four elective courses that add up to at least 13 credits.
Meeting this elective requirement is one of the graduation conditions, along with passing every core course, earning at least 86 credits in total, and finishing with a CGPA of at least 5.0.
Electives are offered in Year 3 Semester 2 and in Year 4.
If you also want a specialization noted on your transcript, at least three of your passed electives must come from the same track.
To get a specialization noted on your transcript, you must pass at least three electives from the same track.
There are three tracks to choose from: AI and Machine Learning, Data Science, and Systems.
Some electives belong to two tracks; each one counts only once toward the elective requirement, but it counts toward every track it belongs to.
Electives start in Year 3, when you can earn a specialization by focusing your electives on one track.
The Industry Internship (CS 499) counts as an elective but belongs to no track, so it does not count toward a specialization.

Yes, you can still drop a course in week five, but you can only drop without penalty during the first two weeks of the semester.
Week five is after that two-week window, so the dropped course will show on your transcript as W (withdrawn).
A course marked W earns no credits, but it does not affect your CGPA.
A student goes on academic probation when their CGPA is below 5.0 at the end of a semester.
While on probation, a student can register for at most 16 credits and has to meet the faculty advisor before registering.
Probation ends once the CGPA is 5.0 or higher at the end of a semester.
The CGPA is the credit-weighted average of grade points over all graded courses taken so far, and failed attempts count until a pass replaces them.
No. You cannot register for two courses that meet in the same timetable slot in the same semester.
Every course meets in one timetable slot, so two courses meeting at the same time are in the same slot.
If two electives you want clash, you have to pick one of them. The other one may be offered again next year.
Yes, you can register for fewer than 9 credits for medical reasons, but you need approval from the head of department.
Taking this lighter load may delay your graduation.
If you register for 9 credits or more, that is still a normal load, so you do not need this approval.

If you want to drop a course you are already registered for, you can do so without penalty only during the first two weeks of the semester. After that, the course shows as W (withdrawn) on your transcript and earns no credits, but it does not affect your CGPA.

Registration closes one week after the next semester starts.

A grade of P or better also meets the requirement for passing a prerequisite.
